item: Filing-deadline arithmetic used a clock typed into the source file
why_flagged: scripts/report_availability.py compared every filing deadline with a hard-coded 04:45 on 2026-11-14 instead of the stamp of the report it was reading, so its verdict ('zero teams are overdue') was produced by the assumption and could never have detected the staleness in F26. It also quoted the game-day filing clause (11 a.m.-1 p.m. local) and then never applied it.
action_needed: The stamp is now read from the snapshot manifest and all three clauses are applied, using worst-case ET ordering rather than a published offset.

item: The injuries page asserted 'no movement at all' as a fixed sentence
why_flagged: The freshness paragraph was a hardcoded literal: it printed 'An overnight gap of nine hours ... produced no movement at all, which is why these rows can be published as settled for today' regardless of the data, and the numbers around it fell back to n/a and 0 when the snapshot carried no prior-report fields. After the refresh the sentence was still there and was false.
action_needed: Every value in that paragraph is now read from the snapshot and the reconciliation, and the 11/14 filing sentence is derived from the availability rows.

item: games_fully_priced_on_availability was computed over dates, not games
why_flagged: The expression grouped states by date and then tested `all(... for rows if date==d)` on the date key, so it could not distinguish a fully-priced game from a partly-priced one and reported 0 of 27 in both states.
action_needed: Grouped by game_id instead; the figure is now 4 of 27, which is the correct count (the four 11/14 games where both sides have filed).

item: The 'back-to-back correspondence' was gated on as a pass condition
why_flagged: report_availability.py returned exit 1 unless the unfiled teams were exactly the back-to-back teams. That was true of the 04:15-05:15 AM reports and is expected to stop being true once those teams file, so the gate would have failed a correct refresh - or, worse, invited a session to keep an old snapshot to keep the gate green.
action_needed: The correspondence is published as an observation about the old snapshot; the gate now checks the real invariant (a team is never published as overdue unless its deadline really has passed).
